chunks: From him, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Qasim, from Safwan al-Jammal, who said:

I witnessed Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) facing the Qiblah before the Takbir, and he said: 'O Allah, do not deprive me of Your Spirit, nor make me despair of Your Mercy, nor make me secure from Your Deceit, for none feel secure from the Deceit of Allah except the losing people.'

I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you, I have not heard this from anyone before you.' So he said: 'Indeed, among the greatest of the major sins in the presence of Allah is hopelessness from the Spirit of Allah, and despair from the Mercy of Allah, and security from the Deceit of Allah.'

key_terms.رَوْحِكَ: Your Spirit (referring to divine life-force or mercy)

ai.seo_question: What is the supplication recited before prayer and what are the three major sins mentioned?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi, this hadith highlights Imam al-Sadiq’s (peace be upon him) emphasis on *al-amn min makr Allah* (false security from God's plan) as a major sin, a concept deeply rooted in Shia theological reflections on divine balance between mercy and majesty. The supplication serves as a spiritual safeguard against complacency, reminding the believer that even amidst divine grace, one must remain vigilant against the subtle deceptions of the self and the world. This teaching underscores the Shia emphasis on *tawhid* in attributes, where recognizing God's comprehensive power prevents both despair and arrogance.

en.hubeali: From him, from his father, form Abdullah Bin Al Qasim, from Safwan Al Jammal who said,

‘I witnessed Abu Abdullahasws and heasws was facing the Qiblah, before the exclamation of Takbeer (to commence the Salāt), and heasws said: ‘O Allahazwj! Do not Let me lose hope from Yourazwj Spirit, nor despair from Yourazwj mercy, nor feel safe from Yourazwj Plan, for there would not feel safe from the Plan of Allahazwj except for the people incurring losses’.

I said, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! I have not heard this from anyone (else) before you<sup>asws</sup>’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘From the most grievous of the major sins in the Presence of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> is the hopelessness from the Spirit of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, and the despair from the Mercy of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, and the (feeling of) security from the Plan of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 3. It is narrated from him (narrator of the Hadith above) from his father from ‘Abd Allah ibn al-Qasim from Safwan al-Jammal who has said the following:

“I observed abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) facing the Qiblah (direction of Ka’bah) before saying Takbir (Allah is greater than can be described) saying, ‘O Lord, do not cause me to lose hope in Your favors and to despair me of Your kindness, or become careless about Your displeasure; no one except the losing people become careless toward the displeasure of Allah.’

I then said, ‘May Allah keep my soul in service for your cause, I have not heard this from anyone before.’ The Imam said, ‘Of the greatest major sins before Allah is to lose hope of the favors of Allah, despair of the mercy of Allah and to become careless about the displeasure of Allah.’”
